title: La Chama: la forma que no se deja poseer

narrative.source_locator: Roberto Pineda Giraldo, La chama, un mito guajiro, Revista de Folklore 2, diciembre de 1947, pp. 113-126; reproducción secundaria searchable en FLACSO Andes.

events.description: La Chama pertenece a peñascos y cuevas y no conserva una única forma.
events.source: Relato vigente y Pineda Giraldo: anciana, majayura, tigre, huevo o flor; no todas las formas pertenecen a cada episodio.

events.description: Un cuidador de caballos encuentra a una joven que pregunta por un burro perdido y la sigue.
events.source: Núcleo narrativo documentado en La chama, un mito guajiro.

events.description: La joven conduce al hombre a una cueva organizada como casa y dominio familiar.
events.source: Núcleo narrativo documentado; el diseño espacial se apoya en la Biblia visual sin universalizar arquitectura.

events.description: La Chama impide que su familia mate al hombre y sale con él.
events.source: Núcleo narrativo documentado; se representa protección y escape sin amenaza gráfica.

events.description: La pareja tiene un hijo; más tarde el hombre inicia otra relación y La Chama se marcha con el niño.
events.source: Síntesis narrativa publicada basada en la continuidad del cuento; no moraliza la ruptura.

events.description: El burro deteriorado, las ollas, la esterilla y la ropa gastada cambian mientras La Chama avanza.
events.source: Transformación material atribuida al episodio; correspondencia uno a uno, sin abundancia inventada.

events.description: El hombre sigue a La Chama durante cinco días y noches hasta lastimarse los pies.
events.source: Corrección de reauditoría: quien sigue es el hombre; la distancia se narra sin violencia gráfica.

events.description: La Chama cuida los pies del hombre y lo esconde de sus parientes en la cueva.
events.source: Pasaje del relato reproducido en fuente secundaria searchable; sin instrucción medicinal ni detalle corporal.

events.description: Mientras La Chama duerme, su familia encuentra al hombre y al hijo; la imagen sólo muestra ausencias posteriores.
events.source: El desenlace violento se conserva en la voz y se elide visualmente: sin cuerpos, sangre, armas, fuego ni preparación de carne.

events.description: La Chama despierta, comprende la pérdida y el conflicto dispersa a su familia sobrenatural.
events.source: La página vigente combina versiones; se evita inventar persecución o combate cuando la fuente secundaria consultada termina en la pérdida.

events.description: La historia revela a una figura que protege, abandona, vuelve a cuidar y pierde, irreductible a seductora o monstruo.
events.source: Tesis editorial vigente que distingue a La Chama de Pülowi y de la majayura de Puró.

events.description: Buscar sus cabellos como remedio repite la idea de que una parte de La Chama puede tomarse sin relación ni límite.
events.source: Creencia histórica registrada, presentada sin receta, eficacia médica ni extracción visible.

story_thesis: La Chama no puede reducirse a una forma, un estereotipo ni una parte apropiable: su ambivalencia pertenece a relaciones, pérdidas y límites inscritos en el territorio.
palette: Warm sand, muted clay red, pale ochre, raw cream, smoky blue, deep indigo and restricted charcoal matte paper. Day and night alternate through broad sky layers. Clay red belongs to La Chama's young garment; charcoal belongs to her elderly garment, hair and cave depth. No glow, glitter, neon, colorful aura, generic particles or uniform darkness.
shared_scene_continuity: ALL PEOPLE are nearly FLAT cut-paper silhouettes with natural proportions for age, contour-profile noses, tiny cut eyes and NO faceted, sculpted, doll-like or Pixar heads.

Full figures remain complete inside frame and usually 8–22% of image height. Compose visually rich environmental depth with foreground, action plane, architecture and distant territory; never default to portrait close-ups.

EVERY visible surface belongs to the papercut world: broad thin matte paper sheets, crisp cut edges, narrow physical air gaps and real cast shadows BETWEEN layers. No photoreal soil, skin, rock, wood, fibre, pottery, fur or straw.

Depth comes from flat planes held at different distances, never thick folded cardboard sculptures. No visible diorama base, external frame, raw cardboard edge, corrugated board, glue, studio table or miniature-box presentation.
Only listed entities may appear. Traditional Wayuu clothing is complete and varied; no loincloth-only styling, generic tribal costume, invented face paint, feathers or fantasy jewelry.

Magic is the story-specific physical behavior of form, cave, path, cargo, care, absence and boundary. No sparkles, glowing dust, constellations, portals, halos, smoke creatures or mystical UI symbols.
continuity_rules: La Chama appears in exactly ONE bodily form per scene. Young and elderly forms never coexist; animal, egg and flower are partial cut apertures or ribbon glimpses, never additional bodies or hybrids.
The man, child, new partner and four relatives keep their exact silhouette and complete clothing. No sexualized framing, loincloth-only figure, invented face paint or generic tribal costume.
The transformed donkey is the same single animal. Every cargo change is one-to-one: three pots become three bags, one mat remains one mat, one full garment remains one full garment.
The man follows La Chama, not the reverse. Five days and nights are exactly five path bands, never five copies of a person.
Care is shown through ground seams beside covered feet. No wound, licking, medicine, dosage, efficacy claim or clinical procedure.
The violent loss remains entirely outside the image. Only two clean absences may persist; no corpse, child harm, blood, meat, bone, knife, pot, flame, attack shadow or ghost.
The later pursuit varies across versions. The video uses empty diverging paths and never asserts a specific chase, transformation combat or winner.
Hair always remains attached to the elderly La Chama and becomes inaccessible cliff strata. No extraction, cutting, remedy preparation or medical promise.

notes: Los 17 modelos canónicos, su hoja de contacto y los tres trípticos del mito fueron inspeccionados visualmente.
La Biblia fija identidades, ropa, objetos y lógica espacial, pero su volumen fotográfico no se copia: los keyframes reconstruyen todo como hojas planas separadas con aire.
Los trípticos aportan escala territorial, pliegues de cueva y motivos de transformación; el video añade continuidad uno a uno y evita símbolos genéricos.
La forma vieja y la joven jamás comparten plano; tigre, huevo y flor no se convierten en reparto.
No se sube ninguna referencia local al proveedor; todo se reconstruye mediante texto.

inventory.desc: ONE and only one young-adult appearance of La Chama per applicable scene: nearly flat paper silhouette, natural proportions, long ankle-length CLAY-RED Wayuushein with small high neck and sleeves to wrists over a SAND chest layer, dark waireña-style sandals, one long black braid. Calm agency, no seductive pose, cleavage, jewelry, face paint, headdress or duplication.

ONE and only one elderly appearance of La Chama per applicable scene: vigorous nearly flat paper silhouette, natural elderly posture, ankle-length CHARCOAL Wayuushein with full sleeves over MUTED OCHRE chest layer, dark sandals, very long black-grey hair remaining attached to her head and reaching her ankles. No witch caricature, nudity, glowing eyes, jewelry, face paint or duplication.

ONE adult Wayuu horse caretaker, nearly flat paper silhouette with natural proportions: long-sleeved DEEP INDIGO Kemiisa, SAND ankle-length Kotin over a safe base, narrow muted sash, dark waireña-style sandals and functional sand hat. Same identity through encounter, partnership, walking and protected guest states; never shirtless, loincloth-only, armed in hand or duplicated.

ONE Wayuu child with child proportions, small nearly flat silhouette, long-sleeved MUTED GREEN Kemiisa, safe sand lower layer, narrow sash and sandals. Distinct from the adult man; never a miniature adult, hybrid, exposed, harmed or duplicated.

Exactly FOUR recurring adult relatives shown only when listed: two women in distinct full ankle-length smoky-blue and muted-ochre Wayuushein; one man in cream long shirt with clay She'etebe; one man in indigo Kemiisa with sand Kotin. Nearly flat full paper figures, separate silhouettes, restrained tension by spacing. No monster anatomy, uniforms, face paint, weapons, food preparation or duplicates.

ONE adult Wayuu woman, nearly flat complete silhouette, ankle-length MUTED OCHRE Wayuushein with full sleeves over indigo chest layer and dark sandals. Self-possessed, not villainized, sexualized or duplicated.

The SAME single small donkey before change: spare but not abused, head lowered, uneven muted-grey cut-paper coat and worn simple rope harness. No wounds, ribs emphasized, saddle, cargo duplication or photoreal fur.

The SAME single donkey after change: sound and glossy only through smooth deep-indigo and smoky-grey paper planes, head raised and harness intact. No different breed, horse conversion, jewel tack, glow or photoreal fur.

Exactly THREE blackened cooking pots, one large, one medium and one small, each a broad flat charcoal paper silhouette with a simple handle or rim. No flame, food, gore, photoreal clay or extra vessels.

Exactly THREE new plain shoulder bags corresponding one-to-one to the three pots, one large, one medium and one small, made of flat clay-red, cream and indigo paper. Plain fields only: no invented kanaas, logos, text, tassel excess or extra bags.
ONE worn rolled mat as a thin ochre paper weave plane with frayed cut edge, still usable and tied by one fibre. No realistic straw or duplicate roll.
The SAME one mat renewed: a clean, intact muted-ochre paper plane, tightly rolled and joined to its earlier state only by one continuous fibre in transformation scenes.

ONE worn full Wayuushein garment in smoky grey, ankle-length body, small high neck and exactly two sleeves to the wrists, represented as a flat paper clothing silhouette. Never a blanket, poncho, short tunic or duplicate.

The SAME full Wayuushein renewed in muted clay red, ankle-length body, small high neck and exactly two sleeves to the wrists, shown as an intact flat paper garment silhouette. No embroidery or pattern invented.

Exactly FIVE distinct cared-for horses in smoky blue, umber and cream flat-paper profiles, small in the landscape, with simple functional tack only. No riders unless the man is separately listed, no extra herd or photoreal hair.

ONE cave-house within layered ochre peñascos: narrow entrance, broad inner chamber, one smaller recess and a suspended plain hammock suggested by separated matte paper sheets. It is this story's supernatural dwelling, not a universal Wayuu house; no stone texture, cardboard box, masonry or domestic clutter.

Arid La Guajira territory translated entirely into broad matte paper: warm-sand ground ribbons, clay and ochre rock fins, sparse low bifurcated thorn shrubs, pale sky layers and long paths. No saguaro cactus, rosette/agave plants, lush jungle, photographic soil or generic fantasy desert.

ONE continuous thin paper ribbon belonging to La Chama's changing presence. It disappears behind rock folds and briefly exposes cut profiles of flower, egg, feline back and human garment WITHOUT showing multiple bodies together, hybrids, smoke, glow, aura or particle trail.

Exactly FOUR physical fold-lines cross four separate cargo chains and share one cast shadow: donkey state, three pots to three bags, worn mat to intact mat, worn grey Wayuushein to intact clay-red Wayuushein. No instantaneous explosion, glow, levitation or duplicated before-and-after inventory.

ONE long paper path folded into exactly FIVE alternating day-and-night bands, each band physically farther in depth. The path lengthens before the single man; it is time and distance, not a portal, staircase, calendar, text or cosmic effect.

Exactly THREE thin cream paper seams close three cracked lines in the ground beside the man's fully covered feet, translating care without showing a wound, licking, medicine, glowing cure or clinical procedure.

Exactly TWO clean empty recesses after the elided loss: one contains the man's sand hat; the other contains one neatly folded muted-green sleeve-piece associated with the child. No bodies, blood, bones, meat, pots, knives, fire, shadows of attack or ghosts.

The elderly La Chama's own long black-grey hair remains visibly attached to her head, crosses exactly THREE narrow air gaps and continues as three charcoal cliff strata. It establishes boundary and belonging; no cutting, pulling, severed locks, hands taking hair, remedy preparation, text or medical symbolism.

blocks.voice_over: La Chama habitaba peñascos y cuevas. Unos la recordaban como anciana de cabello interminable; otros como joven, felino, huevo o flor. Su forma nunca permanecía quieta.
